facts.statement: The type species Eocursor parvus was described in 2007 by Richard J. Butler, Roger M. H. Smith, and David B. Norman.
facts.quote: The type species, Eocursor parvus, was described in 2007 by Richard J. Butler, Roger M. H. Smith, and David B. Norman.

facts.statement: Eocursor had large hands that resembled those of the Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Its large hands resembled those of the Heterodontosauridae, a clade of primitive ornithischians.

facts.statement: The morphology of Eocursor's triangular teeth suggests it was partially herbivorous.
facts.quote: The morphology of the triangular teeth, not unlike those of an iguana, suggests partial herbivory.

facts.statement: Eocursor's tibia was significantly longer than its femur, indicating it was a swift runner.
facts.quote: The tibia was significantly longer than the femur, indicating it was a swift runner.

facts.statement: Eocursor lived at the beginning of the Jurassic period, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago, between the Hettangian and Sinemurian stages, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 200 a 190 millones de años, entre el Hettangiense y el Sinemuriense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The time range for Eocursor is the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages, from 201.4 to 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The exact age of Eocursor is debated; it was originally interpreted as Late Triassic (around 210 million years ago), but later studies suggest it is Early Jurassic, though independent geochronological support for its assumed age remains lacking.
facts.quote: The exact age of this taxon has been the subject of uncertainty. It was originally interprereted as living during the Late Triassic (Norian age), around 210 million years ago; however, Olsen, Kent & Whiteside (2010) stated that there is no independent geochronological support for its assumed age, and the available data makes it impossible to conclusively determine whether Eocursor is of Triassic or Early Jurassic (potentially as young as Sinemurian) age.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Eocursor (SAM-PK-K8025) was collected in 1993 from the Upper Elliot Formation in Free State, South Africa.
facts.quote: In 1993, the holotype specimen of Eocursor (SAM-PK-K8025) was collected from the Upper Elliot Formation in Free State, South Africa.

facts.statement: Eocursor's limbs are significantly long, similar to those of later heterodontosaurids.
facts.quote: Las extremidades son significativamente largas, como las de los heterodontosáuridos posteriores.

facts.statement: Eocursor possessed unusually large hands capable of grasping objects.
facts.quote: Sus manos inusualmente grandes son capaces de agarrar cosas.

facts.statement: Eocursor's tibia was as long as its femur, indicating it was a fast runner.
facts.quote: La tibia, tan larga como el fémur, indica que fue un corredor rápido.
